text:
Southland Conference launches 2026 football season at Houston event
W. M. Rice
The Southland Conference officially launched the 2026 football season on July 21 with its annual Southland Football Opening Drive, held at the George R. Brown Convention Center in Houston. McNeese was represented by head coach Matt Viator, senior running back Tre'Vonte Citizen, and senior safety Javon Davis.
The event began on Monday with social media content recorded by the league office and continued Tuesday with a day-long series of media rounds involving athletes and coaches. Optimism among the league's ten head coaches was described as high, with some stating it is the best they have seen in years.
"It was great to see three of our teams make the playoffs last season," said Viator. "I've been fortunate to have been in this league for a long time, and the football is really good. I was not surprised it was still at that level when I came back, so hopefully we can continue that. Hopefully our programs will keep investing and will keep getting better and elevate the league to the standard that we think it can become."
Last season, McNeese won four of its final six games, including a victory over nationally ranked Lamar in their finale. The Cardinals were one of three teams advancing to the FCS playoffs alongside league champion Stephen F. Austin (SFA) and Southeastern Louisiana University—marking the first time since 2018 that three conference teams reached postseason play.
Lamar head coach Pete Rossomando said, "Obviously you'd like to see somebody bring back the trophy from Nashville (FCS National Championship). We (the Southland) should be there. We've got Texas and Louisiana with some of the finest football players in the whole country. (The league) has the best players, and in a lot of ways, the best coaches." SFA head coach Colby Carthel added, "I think you're going to see this league elevate and I think it starts with leadership...the commitment to this league...it's at the highest point I think it's ever been."
McNeese will report for fall camp on July 28 ahead of its first practice on July 29; preparations are underway for their August 29 home opener against defending champion SFA. Citizen said, "I believe we've had a really good offseason and getting ourselves prepared well for the season...the goal is to hoist the trophy at the end of the season." Davis added, "There's a difference between being ready and prepared...I want to make sure my guys are prepared...and see consistency." Two preseason league polls are expected within days.
